This would be really nice to have IMO, currently it is pretty tedious to update agents and commands to use new models, especially if you want to change provider. 

A nice extension to this idea would be to be able group aliases to models and opencode could then pick a model at random/roundrobin that matches the requested alias.

You could for example have access to zen, GitHub and OpenAI subs, so 3 different places to access GPT-5.2. A group system could allow for all 3 providers to be used and even mix up different models from those providers. for example

```json
"global_aliases": {
  "cheap": [
    "openai/gpt-5-mini", 
    "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini", 
    "opencode/gtp-5-mini", 
    "github-copilot/grok-code-fast-1"
  ]
},
```

then in your agent front matter you just reference 'cheap' and get any one of the above models

```
---
description: 
  Fast, Cheap agent for short, quick, general purpose tasks
mode: subagent
model: alias/cheap
---
```

@ariane-emory You clearly didn't get my point. Please read the Proposed Improvement and Scope section properly.

What i am mean to say here is, **new users** who are eager to try out the tool, **won't** get into permissions and configuration right off the bat. And the default build agent allows every command to be run without permission. 

Whether users know this or not about build agent, LLMs can and will sometimes, execute improper commands like i have mentioned in my issue. Whether it be hallucination or improper formatting, this is outside of the user's and opencode's control. These things can happen to anyone, inclluding me and you, albeit rarely.

The main reason I am proposing this change is to **protect new users** from this. By making this improvement, we make this behavior as opt-out, which will improve the overall user-friendliness, safety and security of the tool out-of-the-box. 

There onwards, if the user wishes to, they can modify the permissions as per their will through the configuration file. Any incident after this will be the responsibility of the user.

Again, this proposed feature is meant to **improve the out-of-the-box experience the tool provides.** Its only going to provide safer and secure permissions by default.
IDEA has been updated to version 2025.3.2, which resolves this issue.

I see this request as only *partially* covered by the existing issues. The ones linked focus mainly on post-hoc visibility (session summaries, exit stats) or hard controls (spending limits / kill switches).

What this proposal is trying to address is a slightly different problem: **near real-time, in-flow visibility** while work is actively happening. The intent is to prevent surprises before limits are hit, especially for long-running tasks, agents, or high-cost models, rather than just reporting usage after the fact.

In that sense, I see this as complementary and potentially unifying those ideas, shifting cost awareness from reactive to proactive, with a lightweight, always-visible indicator that helps users manage trade-offs as they work.
Just in case, there was a PR for adding ACP backend support: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/5095 that was discounted

My opencode tells me this might be the problem:

> Research Complete: Missing Cerebras in opencode models Output
> Root Cause Identified ✅
> Cerebras is deliberately hidden from the opencode models output because it has autoload: false in the CUSTOM_LOADERS configuration.
> How opencode models Works
> 1. Data Source: The command fetches available models from https://models.dev/api.json (via ModelsDev provider)
> 2. Filtering Logic (in /packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts):
>    - The Provider.list() function calls state() which builds the provider database
>    - Each provider goes through a CUSTOM_LOADERS check
>    - Key condition: A provider is only included if result.autoload === true OR the provider is already explicitly in the config
>    - The code: if (result && (result.autoload || providers[providerID]))
> Why Cerebras is Missing
> The CUSTOM_LOADERS for cerebras in provider.ts lines ~360-370:
> cerebras: async () => {
>   return {
>     autoload: false,  // ← THIS IS THE PROBLEM
>     options: {
>       headers: {
>         "X-Cerebras-3rd-Party-Integration": "opencode",
>       },
>     },
>   }
> }
> This means:
> - ✅ Cerebras IS in models.dev
> - ✅ Cerebras SDK IS bundled (@ai-sdk/cerebras)
> - ✅ Cerebras HAS a custom loader configured
> - ❌ But autoload: false causes it to be filtered out UNLESS explicitly added to config
> Comparison with Other Providers
> Providers that DO appear in opencode models have autoload: true:
> - amazon-bedrock: autoload: true (when AWS credentials detected)
> - google-vertex: autoload: true (when GCP_PROJECT env var set)
> Providers that DON'T appear have autoload: false:
> - cerebras: autoload: false
> - openai: autoload: false
> - openrouter: autoload: false
> - azure: autoload: false
> Why This Design?
> This is intentional filtering, not a bug:
> - Providers with autoload: false require explicit API keys or configuration
> - They're only shown in the models list if explicitly enabled in opencode.json
> - This reduces clutter for users who don't have credentials for every provider
> Solution Options
> To show Cerebras models, you need to explicitly add it to your config:
> Edit /Users/janni/.config/opencode/opencode.work.json:
> {
>   provider: {
>     cerebras: {
>       models: {}
>     }
>   }
> }
> Or add it to enabled_providers:
> {
>   enabled_providers: [anthropic, openai, cerebras]
> }
> Summary
> - Root Cause: autoload: false in CUSTOM_LOADERS configuration
> - Why it's filtered: By design - only autoload providers are shown without explicit config
> - Fix: Add cerebras to your opencode.json provider config with API key
> - The "bug": Arguably, the UX is confusing - users expect to see providers that exist in models.dev without needing to know about the autoload mechanism
>

Based on my search, I found related PRs that touch on session compaction, but none appear to be direct duplicates of PR #10380:

**Related but not duplicates:**

1. **PR #7104** - feat(compaction): Hybrid compaction pipeline with deterministic extraction + LLM
   - Related to compaction logic but focuses on a different approach (hybrid pipeline)

2. **PR #6562** - fix(session): prevent context overflow by adding safety margin to compaction check
   - Related to session compaction but addresses a different issue (safety margins)

3. **PR #10363** - Docs: Comprehensive analysis & fix guides for ALL 10 issues
   - Documentation PR that may reference issue #10342 but is not a duplicate

**Conclusion:**
No duplicate PRs found

## Security Consideration
I'm aware of #8313 and the related PR #8727 addressing path traversal via symlinks.
**This PR does not introduce security vulnerabilities:**
1. **No changes to containment checks** - The `Instance.containsPath(resolved)` check (line 355) remains untouched and executes *before* any symlink handling.
2. **Metadata only** - Our change only determines if a symlink points to a directory for display purposes (`type: "directory"` vs `type: "file"`). It does not read file contents or bypass access controls.
3. **Symlink escape still blocked** - If a symlink inside the project points outside (e.g., `evil-link -> /etc`), any attempt to `File.list("evil-link")` will fail at the `containsPath()` check.
4. **Orthogonal to #8727** - PR #8727 adds `realpath()` validation before access. Our change operates *after* containment is verified, only affecting how entries are classified in listings.
The existing path-traversal tests in `test/file/path-traversal.test.ts` continue to pass.
